journal_name: CCF Transactions on Pervasive Computing and Interaction

abstracts.abstract: Current context-aware systems predominantly rely on static context models that fail to capture the inherently dynamic and interconnected nature of human activities in smart environments. This paper introduces a novel theoretical framework termed Dynamic Context Topology (DCT) for pervasive computing, which conceptualizes contextual information as a continuously evolving graph structure rather than discrete attribute-value pairs. Unlike conventional context models that treat environmental factors as independent variables, DCT explicitly models the temporal dependencies and spatial correlations among contextual elements through dynamic graph neural mechanisms. We formalize the context inference process using probabilistic temporal logic and derive optimal sensing policies based on information-theoretic principles. The theoretical analysis demonstrates that DCT achieves a theoretical bound of O(log n) improvement in context recognition accuracy compared to traditional Bayesian approaches, where n represents the number of contextual entities. Furthermore, we prove that the framework exhibits provable convergence properties under non-stationary environmental conditions, addressing a fundamental limitation of existing context-aware systems. This work represents a paradigm shift from input-output context processing toward holistic, topology-aware contextual reasoning, opening new research directions for ambient intelligence systems that fundamentally transform how machines perceive and respond to human needs in pervasive computing environments.

Predicting user behavior in mobile computing scenarios remains challenging due to the inherent complexity of modeling sequential patterns under resource constraints. This paper presents an Enhanced Hierarchical Contextual Hidden Markov Model (EHCHMM) that significantly advances the state-of-the-art by incorporating deep contextual embeddings into the classical hidden Markov framework. Unlike prior approaches that treat context as external observations, EHCHMM integrates learned contextual representations as latent state modifiers, enabling more nuanced modeling of user intentions across diverse interaction modalities. We derive closed-form solutions for model parameters using variational EM inference, substantially reducing computational complexity from O(n³) to O(n² log n) while maintaining prediction accuracy. Theoretical analysis establishes tight bounds on the generalization error, demonstrating that the proposed model achieves regret bounds that are √d times smaller than baseline methods, where d represents the embedding dimensionality. Extensive analysis across multiple real-world datasets validates that EHCHMM reduces prediction latency by 47% while improving accuracy by 23% compared to existing contextual bandit approaches. The framework provides rigorous theoretical guarantees for adaptive systems operating in resource-constrained mobile and wearable computing environments, advancing the foundations of context-aware mobile services.

Existing human-computer interaction paradigms in smart environments remain fundamentally reactive, responding to user commands after they are issued. This paper presents IntentIO, a pioneering intention-driven interaction system that fundamentally transforms the paradigm from reactive command processing to proactive need anticipation in pervasive computing contexts. The system architecture comprises three novel components: a Multi-Modal Intention Anticipator that fuses physiological signals, environmental context, and historical behavior patterns; a Temporal Intention Graph that maintains probabilistic relationships between user goals and environmental states; and a Proactive Service Orchestrator that initiates appropriate interventions before explicit user requests. The system implements a closed-loop feedback mechanism where confirmed intentions reinforce predictive models while unconfirmed predictions trigger uncertainty-aware backoff strategies. Through a 12-week deployment study involving 86 participants across residential and office smart environments, IntentIO demonstrated the capability to correctly anticipate user intentions with 91.3% accuracy an average of 4.7 minutes before explicit requests. Notably, the system achieved a 73% reduction in perceived task completion latency and significantly improved user satisfaction scores in the System Usability Scale. This work establishes a new interaction paradigm for ambient intelligence, demonstrating that proactive intention-aware systems can fundamentally enhance the human experience in ubiquitous computing environments.

Energy consumption remains a critical bottleneck for continuous physiological monitoring in wearable computing devices, limiting the utility of health-focused IoT applications. This paper presents AdaptSense, an adaptive sensing framework that substantially improves upon existing duty-cycling approaches through intelligent sensor scheduling based on physiological coherence detection. The system employs a lightweight neural network classifier that operates directly on sensor raw data to detect periods of physiological stability, adjusting sampling rates accordingly without requiring cloud offloading. AdaptSense introduces a novel coherence-aware scheduling algorithm that maintains monitoring fidelity during dynamic periods while aggressively reducing sampling during stable phases. The implementation operates within 8KB of RAM on ARM Cortex-M4 microcontrollers, demonstrating practical deployability on resource-constrained wearable platforms. Evaluation across 24-hour continuous monitoring scenarios with 34 participants shows that AdaptSense achieves 89% energy reduction compared to fixed-rate sampling while preserving 96.4% of clinically relevant physiological events. The system demonstrates robust performance across diverse activities including sedentary work, exercise, and sleep, with graceful degradation handling when physiological signal quality degrades. This work provides a practical solution for extending wearable device battery life by an order of magnitude, enabling truly continuous health monitoring in pervasive IoT ecosystems.
